bibliographic.title: Analysis of Data Management in Blockchain-Based Systems: From Architecture to Governance
bibliographic.authors: Paik, H.-Y., Xu, X., Bandara, H. M. N. D., Lee, S. U., & Lo, S. K.
bibliographic.citation_apa: Paik, H.-Y., Xu, X., Bandara, H. M. N. D., Lee, S. U., & Lo, S. K. (2019). Analysis of data management in blockchain-based systems: From architecture to governance. IEEE Access, 7, 186091-186113. https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2019.2961404

methodology.study_design: developer-oriented conceptual analysis of blockchain as a data store within larger software systems
methodology.sector: blockchain technology; distributed data management; software architecture
methodology.technology_context: blockchain-based systems as distributed immutable data stores with on-chain/off-chain data architecture; tangential references to machine learning and deep learning in blockchain analytics contexts

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article analyzes blockchain data management and blockchain data governance (privacy, quality assurance), not conversational governance, LLM-based systems, chatbots, agents, or related operational controls in generative AI deployments.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Provided text identifies the study as a conceptual analysis of blockchains from a developer viewpoint, covering architectural layers, data placement/flow, data administration, blockchain analytics, and data governance for privacy and quality assurance. Mentions of machine learning, deep learning, compliance, audit, and regulated sectors appear only as peripheral blockchain application or reference contexts, not as LLM or conversational-system governance evidence. The work predates and does not address LLM-specific governance mechanisms required by the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Technology focus and absence of conversational AI or LLM governance are explicit in title, abstract, and introduction.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects a 2019 conceptual/architectural blockchain paper. Empirical sampling, ethics, and limitations are not substantively described in the provided excerpts. Method fit is adequate for its stated conceptual aim but not for empirical causal inference.

cerqual.explanation: Within its own domain the paper presents a coherent developer-oriented blockchain data-management framework, but methodological depth for empirical claims is limited in the provided text. Relevance to conversational governance in LLM systems in regulated environments is very low because the governance focus is blockchain data privacy and quality assurance, not generative or conversational AI oversight.

coding.subtheme: Architectural and administrative analysis of blockchain as a component data store

synthesis.main_claim: Blockchains should be understood and incorporated as distributed data stores within larger software systems through structured architectural, administrative, analytic, and governance considerations.
synthesis.contribution: Conceptualizes blockchain layers in software architecture, examines data placement and flow, discusses blockchain data administration and trustable analytics, and outlines governance issues around privacy and quality assurance.
synthesis.limitations: Provided excerpts do not detail study limitations; empirical validation, conversational AI applicability, and LLM governance are not addressed.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central or supporting evidence on conversational governance in LLM systems. At most, marginal foundational context only if the review separately maps distributed auditability and data-governance concepts to non-LLM infrastructures.
